glosses: Capable of being pulled or stretched into thin wire by mechanical force without breaking.

examples.text: ductile material

ductile alloy
ductile state
Gold is highly ductile, allowing it to be drawn into very fine wires.
The ductile nature of copper makes it essential in electrical wiring.

glosses: Molded easily into a new form.

examples.text: their organisation was, by hereditary culture, much more ductile and more readily capable of acquiring knowledge than mine.

glosses: Led easily; prone to follow.

translations.source_sense_description: leicht zu biegen, elastisch; von Personen: beweglich, gelenkig

glosses: Capable of being flexed or bent without breaking; able to be turned or twisted without breaking.

examples.text: When the splitting wind Makes flexible the knees of knotted oaks.

glosses: Willing or prone to give way to the influence of others; not invincibly rigid or obstinate.

examples.text: Phocion the Athenian (a man of great severity, and no ways flexible to the will of the people[…]

glosses: Capable of adapting or changing to suit new or modified conditions or situations.

examples.text: You can't always get what you want: you need to learn to be flexible.

glosses: Capable or being adapted or molded in some way.

glosses: Something that is flexible.

examples.text: Alcan is mostly flexibles -- and so it boosts Amcor's flexible packaging business to a globally significant $7 billion one.
